findings.current: In one word, he was a born talent.
findings.defect: “Born talent” reduces Choi’s advantage to innate ability, while 준비된 인재 summarizes the combination of his natural martial talent and the substantial energy already accumulated inside him.
findings.rationale: The preceding sentences identify two separate advantages—innate martial talent and preexisting internal energy—which 준비된 captures as preparation or readiness.
findings.replacement: In short, he was a talent with all the groundwork already laid.
findings.source: 한 단어로 정리하자면, 준비된 인재라는 거다.

findings.current: “No. I’m worried because it seems one of our Guild members is about to put himself in danger.”
findings.defect: The draft makes the Guild member deliberately place himself in danger, whereas 위험에 빠지다 only says that he appears to be heading into or falling into danger.
findings.rationale: The source expresses Choi’s concern about Jin’s peril without explicitly assigning deliberate agency to Jin.
findings.replacement: “No. I’m worried because it looks like one of our Guild members is heading into danger.”
findings.source: “그건 아니고, 길드원 중 하나가 위험에 빠지는 것 같아서 걱정이 되네요.”

findings.defect: The draft reads 멀리 안 나갑니다 literally as a statement about Jin’s future location. In this departure exchange, it is the conventional remark that he will not accompany the visitor farther or see him out.
findings.rationale: Choi has just risen to leave while Jin remains behind to cultivate; the line dismisses him without escorting him out.
findings.replacement: “All right. I won’t see you out.”

findings.current: “I’m not concerned about that. I understand that it is Mr. Johnson’s way of expressing familiarity. This concerns Guild business.”
findings.defect: “Expressing familiarity” is an unnatural and overly literal rendering of 친밀감 표현, obscuring Choi’s dry acknowledgment that Johnson behaves that way to show closeness.
findings.rationale: 친밀감 here means affectionate closeness or fondness, and 그보다는 explicitly pivots to the more pertinent Guild matter.
findings.replacement: “I’m not concerned about that. I know that’s simply Mr. Johnson’s way of showing affection. More importantly, this concerns Guild business.”
findings.source: “신경 안 씁니다. 미스터 존슨 나름대로의 친밀감 표현이라는 걸 알고 있으니까요. 그보다는 길드 업무 관련 내용입니다.”

findings.current: The wheels of a tank, made of countless footsteps and metal, crushed the feathers as they drifted back down.
findings.defect: The draft grammatically makes a tank consist of “countless footsteps and metal,” eliminating the marching feet as a separate agent that tramples the feathers.
findings.rationale: The source names two things trampling the falling feathers: countless footsteps and the wheels of metal tanks.
findings.replacement: Countless marching feet and the metal wheels of tanks crushed the feathers as they fluttered down.
findings.source: 흐느적거리며 추락한 깃털을 짓밟은 것은 수많은 걸음과 금속으로 이루어진 전차의 바퀴였다.

findings.current: “He could have lived if he hadn’t given up until the very end. He should have fought with everything he had somehow. That sort of thing.”
findings.defect: The draft invents and repeatedly specifies a singular male subject, narrowing the source’s omitted subject and changing the movie reference’s survival consequence.
findings.rationale: The Korean leaves the subject unstated, while the surrounding speech turns the movie’s collective lesson into encouragement for the assembled troops; the explicit singular “he” is unsupported.
findings.replacement: “They could have lived if they hadn’t given up until the very end. They should have fought with everything they had, no matter what. That sort of thing.”
findings.source: “마지막까지 포기하지 않았으면 살 수 있었을 텐데. 어떻게든 죽을힘을 다해 싸웠어야지. 뭐 그런 생각.”

summary: The draft contains two scene-fact errors and several meaningful losses of characterization or pragmatic meaning.
